title: The Oath of Caerlum
premise: The Guild of Caerlum trades in impossible things—bottled echoes, borrowed luck, the last hour of a dying man—and Petra Hartwell, its youngest and last true member, keeps the ledgers that prove it all happened. When prayers to forgotten gods start being answered across the city, the guild's carefully maintained invisibility shatters: a royal inquisitor arrives hunting the 'door out of Vessany,' a country erased from maps forty years ago, and every ledger entry points back to Caerlum. Petra must choose between burning the records that preserve her dead mentors' truths or using them to open the door, dragging her ragged found family into a country that exists only because people refused to stop remembering it. In the end, Petra rewrites the final ledger page herself, walks her family through the door as winter closes, and leaves behind a single entry so the next keeper will know the way.
about_author: A. M. Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the paperwork of defunct institutions before turning to fiction. They write about record-keepers, small loyalties, and the strange weight of things that refuse to be forgotten, and live somewhere with long winters.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A quiet night of auditing the guild's storeroom: bottled echoes, a saint's second shadow, debts owed by the dead. Establishes the dying guild's warmth and Petra's devotion to the ledgers. Emotional beat: belonging inside something almost gone.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered in the Fishmarket
chapters.summary: Petra witnesses a fishwife's desperate prayer to a nameless old god actually work—a drowned son walks out of the harbor. The crowd's awe turns fearful. Petra realizes the impossible is leaking into the ordinary. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What Master Corvane Kept Locked
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She finds a sealed ledger in the vault labeled 'Vessany' in her dead mentor's hand. The guild's oldest members refuse to discuss it. First hint the guild didn't just trade in impossibilities—it helped erase one. Emotional beat: betrayal at one remove.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor Arrives on a Grey Horse
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Serah Vole's POV. She enters the city with royal writ and a list of names, hunting those who remember Vessany. Coldly competent, quietly haunted by her own erased hometown. Emotional beat: sympathy for an antagonist.

chapters.title: Ledger Entries That Should Not Exist
chapters.summary: Petra discovers entries in her own handwriting she never wrote—records of a door, dated next spring. The old gods are answering through the books themselves. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past and future are no longer safe places.

chapters.title: The Family You Keep Anyway
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter from the guild cook Bramble's POV: a supper scene among the last members—the forger, the retired thief, the boy who talks to locks. Warmth against encroaching fear. Emotional beat: found family named aloud for the first time.

chapters.title: Questions in a Room Without Echoes
chapters.summary: Serah interrogates the guild under pretext of customs fraud. Petra lies for the first time in her life and is good at it, which frightens her more than the inquisitor does. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth begins its real argument.

chapters.title: The Country That Was Unwritten
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The eldest member, half-mad Odile, finally tells the truth: Vessany wasn't conquered, it was bargained away—its name sold to buy the capital a century without plague. The gods went unpaid. Emotional beat: grief for a home Petra never had.

chapters.title: Winter Comes Early This Year
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. Snow falls in harvest month. Markets fail, prayers multiply, and answered prayers demand payment. The city turns on anyone who looks foreign or remembers too much. Emotional beat: the world tightening like a fist.

chapters.title: A Debt Collected in Bone
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A neighbor's answered prayer takes her daughter instead. Petra sees what the returning gods actually are—not kind, just hungry after forty years of silence. Emotional beat: horror; wonder fully dies.

chapters.title: The Forger's Confession
chapters.summary: The guild forger, Tamsin, admits she has been forging Vessany documents for years—for Serah, before Serah was an inquisitor. Old debts entangle hunter and hunted. Emotional beat: no clean sides, only tangled loyalties.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Are For
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, alone with the archive at night. She understands at last: the ledgers don't record the impossible, they hold it in place. Burn them and Vessany dies forever; keep them and the guild stays a target. Emotional beat: the weight of custody.

chapters.title: Arrest at the Salt Gate
chapters.summary: Odile is taken by Serah's soldiers. The guild debates rescue versus flight; the boy who talks to locks already has a plan nobody approved. Emotional beat: the family fractures over what loyalty requires.

chapters.title: Breaking Into the Question House
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV during the rescue. Locks, lies, and a near-fatal mistake that costs them their safehouse. They get Odile but leave a trail straight back to Caerlum. Emotional beat: victory that feels like a countdown starting.

chapters.title: The Door Out of Vessany
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Following the impossible ledger entries, they find the door: not wood, but a threshold made of accumulated memory, hidden beneath the guild itself. It opens only for those whose names are written in the ledgers. Emotional beat: awe and terror braided together.

chapters.title: Serah Vole Remembers Her Mother's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Interrogating Odile, she touches a ledger page and suddenly remembers Vessany—her own erased childhood, the bargain that bought her career. Her certainty cracks. Emotional beat: an antagonist choosing which truth to serve.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Ensemble. The city starves; mobs burn the archives district. The guild's storeroom of impossible things becomes the last library of Vessany. They load what they can carry. Emotional beat: sacrifice—leaving most of everything behind.

chapters.title: Standoff in the Vault of Names
chapters.summary: Climax part one. Serah corners them at the door with soldiers and a royal order to seal Vessany permanently. Petra offers her the ledger with her mother's name in it. Emotional beat: the argument between law and justice made flesh.

chapters.title: An Entry Written in Two Hands
chapters.summary: Climax part two. Sera lowers her sword, writes her own name into the ledger, and turns on her soldiers. The door opens onto a country that never stopped existing—snowfields, lit windows, waiting people. Emotional beat: catharsis; truth wins by being chosen, not enforced.

chapters.title: Crossing
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The passage costs something from each of them—a memory apiece, taken fairly by the door. Petra gives up her memory of Master Corvane's face, keeping only his lessons. Emotional beat: bittersweet price of beginning again.

chapters.title: A New Ledger, An Old Country
chapters.summary: Resolution. The family settles in returned Vessany; the gods, paid at last, grow quiet and almost kind. Serah becomes the new country's first honest record-keeper of its own erasure. Emotional beat: healing without forgetting.

chapters.title: The Last Page of the Caerlum Ledgers
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Petra's POV. She writes the closing entry and leaves the finished ledger on the far side of the sealed door, where some future keeper in the old country might find it. Final line mirrors the first inventory. Emotional beat: peace; custody passed forward, story complete.
